knowledge:
- key_parameters: max.mismatch=specifies the maximum number of mismatching letters allowed for inexact matching in matchPattern and countPattern ;; fixed=controls whether IUPAC ambiguity codes (like N) are treated as wildcards; can be a logical value or a named logical vector (e.g., c(pattern=FALSE, subject=TRUE)) ;; active=a logical vector or replacement method used to enable or disable specific built-in masks (e.g., "AGAPS", "AMB", "RM", "TRF") on a MaskedDNAString ;; append=logical parameter in file writing to append hits to an existing file or overwrite it
- alternatives: matchPDict / PDict=highly preferred over matchPattern (100x to 10000x faster) when searching for a dictionary of many patterns, but restricted to constant-width (same length) DNA patterns ;; BSgenomeForge=package to use when users need to build/forge their own custom BSgenome data package instead of using pre-built Bioconductor ones
- when_to_use: Use this package when you need to find exact or inexact matches of one or many nucleotide patterns (such as transcription factor binding sites, PCR primers, or restriction sites) across both strands of all chromosomes in a reference genome, with or without masking assembly gaps and repeat regions.
- pitfalls: Do not compute the reverse strand sequence of an entire chromosome using reverseComplement on the subject, as it is highly memory-inefficient; instead, transpose the analysis by taking the reverseComplement of the query pattern ;; Loading all chromosomes into memory simultaneously can cause memory exhaustion; load and analyze one chromosome at a time (e.g., using genome[[seqname]]) ;; Improper use of matchPattern without pre-converting the pattern to the same class as the subject (e.g., DNAString) can degrade performance if the pattern is reused many times ;; When using fixed=FALSE without masking, Ns in the subject (like assembly gaps) are treated as wildcards, leading to an abnormally high number of false matches; keep "AGAPS" and "AMB" masks active or specify fixed=c(pattern=FALSE, subject=TRUE).

workflows.name: variable_length_pattern_search
workflows.intent: Find exact or inexact matches of a set of variable-length nucleotide patterns across both strands of all chromosomes in a genome and write the hits to a tab-delimited file.
input: ce2dict0.fa (FASTA file containing a dictionary of variable-length nucleotide patterns)
workflows.stages: 1. Load the target BSgenome package ;; 2. Read the input query patterns from a FASTA file using readDNAStringSet ;; 3. Iterate through each chromosome, loading it individually to conserve memory ;; 4. For each pattern, find matches on the forward strand using matchPattern ;; 5. Take the reverseComplement of the pattern and find matches on the reverse strand using matchPattern ;; 6. Export the matches (chromosome, start, end, strand, pattern ID) to a tab-separated text file.
workflows.code:
ce2dict0_file <- system.file("extdata", "ce2dict0.fa", package="BSgenome")
ce2dict0 <- readDNAStringSet(ce2dict0_file, "fasta")
writeHits <- function(seqname, matches, strand, file="", append=FALSE)
{
    if (file.exists(file) && !append)
        warning("existing file ", file, " will be overwritten with 'append=FALSE'")
    if (!file.exists(file) && append)
        warning("new file ", file, " will have no header with 'append=TRUE'")
    hits <- data.frame(seqname=rep.int(seqname, length(matches)),
                       start=start(matches),
                       end=end(matches),
                       strand=rep.int(strand, length(matches)),
                       patternID=names(matches),
                       check.names=FALSE)
    write.table(hits, file=file, append=append, quote=FALSE, sep="\t",
                row.names=FALSE, col.names=!append)
}
runAnalysis1 <- function(dict0, outfile="")
{
    library(BSgenome.Celegans.UCSC.ce2)
    genome <- BSgenome.Celegans.UCSC.ce2
    seqnames <- seqnames(genome)
    seqnames_in1string <- paste(seqnames, collapse=", ")
    cat("Target:", metadata(genome)$genome,
        "chromosomes", seqnames_in1string, "\n")
    append <- FALSE
    for (seqname in seqnames) {
        subject <- genome[[seqname]]
        cat(">>> Finding all hits in chromosome", seqname, "...\n")
        for (i in seq_len(length(dict0))) {
            patternID <- names(dict0)[i]
            pattern <- dict0[[i]]
            plus_matches <- matchPattern(pattern, subject)
            names(plus_matches) <- rep.int(patternID, length(plus_matches))
            writeHits(seqname, plus_matches, "+", file=outfile, append=append)
            append <- TRUE
            rcpattern <- reverseComplement(pattern)
            minus_matches <- matchPattern(rcpattern, subject)
            names(minus_matches) <- rep.int(patternID, length(minus_matches))
            writeHits(seqname, minus_matches, "-", file=outfile, append=append)
        }
        cat(">>> DONE\n")
    }
}
runAnalysis1(ce2dict0, outfile="ce2dict0_ana1.txt")

workflows.name: constant_width_dictionary_search
workflows.intent: Efficiently find exact matches for a dictionary of constant-width nucleotide patterns across both strands of all chromosomes using matchPDict.
input: ce2dict0.fa (FASTA file containing nucleotide patterns, which are truncated to a constant width)
workflows.stages: 1. Load the target BSgenome package ;; 2. Read the input query patterns and truncate or ensure they are of constant width using DNAStringSet ;; 3. Build a pattern dictionary index using PDict ;; 4. Iterate through each chromosome ;; 5. Search the forward strand using matchPDict and extract matches with extractAllMatches ;; 6. Search the reverse strand by creating a PDict of the reverseComplement of the dictionary, running matchPDict, and extracting matches ;; 7. Export the hits to a tab-separated text file.
workflows.code:
ce2dict0_file <- system.file("extdata", "ce2dict0.fa", package="BSgenome")
ce2dict0 <- readDNAStringSet(ce2dict0_file, "fasta")
runOneStrandAnalysis <- function(dict0, bsgenome, seqnames, strand,
                                 outfile="", append=FALSE)
{
    cat("\nTarget: strand", strand, "of", metadata(bsgenome)$genome,
        "chromosomes", paste(seqnames, collapse=", "), "\n")
    if (strand == "-")
        dict0 <- reverseComplement(dict0)
    pdict <- PDict(dict0)
    for (seqname in seqnames) {
        subject <- bsgenome[[seqname]]
        cat(">>> Finding all hits in strand", strand, "of chromosome", seqname, "...\n")
        mindex <- matchPDict(pdict, subject)
        matches <- extractAllMatches(subject, mindex)
        writeHits(seqname, matches, strand, file=outfile, append=append)
        append <- TRUE
        cat(">>> DONE\n")
    }
}
runAnalysis2 <- function(dict0, outfile="")
{
    library(BSgenome.Celegans.UCSC.ce2)
    genome <- BSgenome.Celegans.UCSC.ce2
    seqnames <- seqnames(genome)
    runOneStrandAnalysis(dict0, genome, seqnames, "+", outfile=outfile, append=FALSE)
    runOneStrandAnalysis(dict0, genome, seqnames, "-", outfile=outfile, append=TRUE)
}
ce2dict0cw15 <- DNAStringSet(ce2dict0, end=15)
runAnalysis2(ce2dict0cw15, outfile="ce2dict0cw15_ana2.txt")

workflows.name: masked_genome_analysis
workflows.intent: Count pattern occurrences in a masked genome while ignoring assembly gaps, ambiguities, or repeat regions.
workflows.stages: 1. Load the masked genome package ;; 2. Access a specific chromosome (which returns a MaskedDNAString) ;; 3. Activate or deactivate specific built-in masks (such as "AGAPS", "AMB", "RM", "TRF") using active(masks(chr)) ;; 4. Count pattern occurrences using countPattern with mask awareness.
workflows.code:
library(BSgenome.Hsapiens.UCSC.hg38.masked)
genome <- BSgenome.Hsapiens.UCSC.hg38.masked
chrY <- genome$chrY
active(masks(chrY))["RM"] <- TRUE
active(masks(chrY)) <- FALSE
active(masks(chrY))["AGAPS"] <- TRUE
Ebox <- "CANNTG"
active(masks(chrY))[c("AGAPS", "AMB")] <- TRUE
countPattern(Ebox, chrY, fixed=FALSE)
